title: The parables of Jesus
note: A parable is a short story drawn from everyday life (farming, money, family, feasts) that teaches about God and his kingdom. The parables appear in Matthew, Mark and Luke; several of the best known, such as the Good Samaritan and the prodigal son, are found only in Luke.

items.a: a short everyday story that teaches a spiritual truth
d: a prayer said at the temple

items.c: The seed in the parable of the sower (Luke 8)
items.a: the word of God

items.a: sprang up but withered for lack of moisture

faith must be hidden to stay pure

items.c: Leaven parable
items.a: the kingdom spreads like yeast through dough

items.a: a merchant sells all he has to buy one pearl
d: a servant hides a pearl in the ground
a king gives pearls to his guests

items.a: both grow together until the harvest

items.a: hid it in the earth and was rebuked

items.c: Ten virgins: what the foolish five did
items.a: took no oil with their lamps
d: broke their lamps on the way

items.c: The rich fool's plan
items.a: pull down his barns and build greater
d: sell his land and give to the poor
lend his grain at high interest

items.c: Pharisee and publican: who went home justified
items.a: the publican who prayed for mercy
d: the Pharisee who fasted twice a week

items.c: The unmerciful servant
items.a: forgiven a huge debt, he would not forgive a small one
d: he forgave everyone who owed him
he paid his master back twice over

items.c: Laborers in the vineyard
items.a: those hired last were paid the same as the first
d: those hired first were paid double
those hired last were sent away unpaid

items.c: Wise and foolish builders
items.a: the wise built on rock, the foolish on sand
d: the wise built a tower, the foolish a wall

items.c: Rich man and Lazarus
items.a: after death the beggar is comforted, the rich man in torment
d: Jesus raises a rich man's friend from the dead

items.ex: This Lazarus is a character in a story, not Lazarus of Bethany.

items.c: Point of the widow and the unjust judge
items.a: that men ought always to pray, and not to faint
d: that widows should not go to court

read.title: The Good Samaritan (Luke 10:25-37)
text: And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life? He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou? And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself. And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live. But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?

And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead. And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side. And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side. But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him. And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves? And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

q.q: Who asked Jesus the question that led to this parable?
What did the Samaritan give the host of the inn?
What does Jesus tell the questioner at the end?
o: Thy faith hath made thee whole
